Atomically claim a release spotlight and mark its visible digest as

spotlight receipt. Exactly one concurrent request can therefore win on
databases that support ``SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`` (including production
PostgreSQL). SQLite uses ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` before the read to provide the

later generic preference merge cannot replace an entire receipt map.

backward-compat carrier (older frontends; in-flight installs across the deploy)
and its absence is now non-fatal. The install stays 2.3.1-compliant either way
(no manual domain entry).

Create a new SEO analysis for a company profile.

This endpoint:
1. Validates user has access to the company profile
2. Validates workflow prerequisite (current_step >= 2)
3. Creates the SEO analysis record with status='pending'
4. Launches background task via TaskSupervisor
5. Returns the analysis record immediately

Frontend should then:
- Poll GET /api/seo/analysis/{analysis_id} for status updates

The analysis process includes:
- Collecting SEO data from crawled pages
- Fetching Core Web Vitals from PageSpeed API
- Calculating scores across multiple categories
- Generating actionable recommendations

Prerequisites:
- Workflow must be at Step 2 or later (current_step >= 2)
- This ensures web crawl inventory data is available for analysis

Args:
    request_data: SEOAnalysisCreate with company_profile_id and primary_url
    current_user: Authenticated user
    db: Database session

Returns:
    SEOAnalysisResponse with analysis record (status='pending')

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 if company profile not found, 403 if access denied,
                  400 if workflow prerequisite not met

``relative_delta`` is null when the baseline is ~0 (an honest "new/!comparable",
never a fabricated %); ``data_sufficiency`` is ``ok`` once the window has enough
days, else ``insufficient`` (e.g. WoW with under a full prior week).

CampaignOptimizationChange.title: CampaignOptimizationChange
CampaignOptimizationChange.description:
One concrete change inside a pending optimization, for a before/after review.

Carries the data-backed *why* (``rationale``) and the list of literal field/asset
``edits`` (each a clean before -> after), so accepting a live-campaign change is
informed -- the reviewer sees exactly which fields/assets change and the reason.

CampaignOptimizationFieldEdit.title: CampaignOptimizationFieldEdit
CampaignOptimizationFieldEdit.description:
One concrete field/asset edit, as a clean before -> after mapping.

Sourced from a single ``optimization_action`` (not the option-level prose), so
each row is the literal thing changing: a copy field (headline/description) with
its current vs proposed text, the new creative image, or a keyword operation
(pause / add / add-negative) with the metric evidence behind it.

CampaignOptimizationSummary.title: CampaignOptimizationSummary
CampaignOptimizationSummary.description:
A per-campaign rollup of AI-team activity, keyed by the campaign's public id.

``campaign_id`` is the same public id the dashboard exposes on each card
(``ads_<hash>`` for paid, ``social_<hash>`` / ``batch_<hash>_<platform>`` for
social), so the frontend can merge this onto a card with a direct lookup.

CampaignPendingRecommendation.title: CampaignPendingRecommendation
CampaignPendingRecommendation.description:
A still-open AI-team optimization the user can Accept/Decline from the card.

Sourced from an ``AgentTeamApproval`` in an OPEN state (pending/deferred/
escalated) whose decision payload references this campaign. ``approval_id`` +
``team_id`` are what the frontend passes to the approvals decision endpoint,
so the card never has to resolve the active team itself.

CampaignPerfHistoryPoint.title: CampaignPerfHistoryPoint

``value`` is null on a day with no spend (an honest gap, not a fabricated zero).

CampaignPerfRevision.title: CampaignPerfRevision
CampaignPerfRevision.description:
One entry in the campaign's optimization/revision history: what the AI changed, when, and the
measured before/after result. Built entirely from data we already store (the action's
change_from/change_to + the per-optimization metric snapshots) -- a real "what was it, what did we
change, did it work" trail without any new capture layer.

FirstPartyBuyerTargetRequest.title: FirstPartyBuyerTargetRequest
FirstPartyBuyerTargetRequest.description:
The velocity a retail buyer actually expects, as stated by the marketer.

This is the one number on the sales surface that no file contains and no
model can infer. A buyer's hurdle rate is a commercial term one retailer
imposed on one brand in one review cycle, so it arrives by being typed, and
every figure downstream of it is only as good as its provenance.

`source` is therefore REQUIRED and not defaulted. A target with no stated
origin is indistinguishable, three months later, from a number somebody
guessed, and it drives the gap and the size of the prize on a screen a
marketer quotes to that same buyer.

Send `unit_per_store_per_week: null` to clear the target and fall back to
the modelled percentile.
